Let me take you through the developments across our business segments, starting with Ash & 
Coal Handling. India's growing power demand, continued dependence on the thermal power 
generation and plan for further increase of the capacity to 150 gigawatts in the coal-based power 
plant by 2035 compared to earlier envisaged 97-gigawatts, continue to provide strong structural 
growth opportunity for our business. 
 
Stricter environmental compliance requirement and financial consequence of non-compliance 
are also making the ash management and complete ash utilization a critical operational 
necessities for the thermal power plant and accelerating the shift towards outsourcing to 
organized players with proven execution capabilities, strong logistic infrastructure and robust 
compliance credentials. 
 
This quarter of the year has always been tough for us with monsoon conditions in Northeast and 
Central part of India, directly impacting our execution volume and consequently impacting the 
revenue due to rainfall, water logging and transportation constraint temporarily reducing our 
volume, which we handle on a day-to-day basis. 
 
Therefore, quarterly performance needs to be viewed in the context of seasonal operating 
conditions. Despite these weather-related challenges, we have made a healthy year-on-year 
progress with revenue up by 36% and PAT up by 13% in the Q2FY27and PAT up by 56% in 
H1 FY27on year-to-year basis. 
 
This reflects the strength of our underlying business, execution capabilities and growing our 
order pipeline. As conditions bounce back, our focus remains on accelerating the executions, 
mobilizing new secured orders and converting opportunity into profitable growth. 
 
The focus on developing integrated ash handling contracts has been high and we are working in 
multiple states to convert the opportunity to order. We'll continue to exercise discipline in our

bidding and pricing and commercial arrangement with these GENCOs with an emphasis on this

Moving to our next area of focus, I'd like to highlight our entry into ready-mix concrete business, 
an important strategic step that represents a natural forward integration for our existing ash 
handling business. 
 
By extending our presence downstream into the construction material and infrastructure 
ecosystem, we aim to strengthen ash utilization, access new markets, create complementary 
avenues for the growth. While leveraging our existing expertise in logistics and material 
handling and industrial operations to build an integrated presence across the value chain. 
 
The Indian RMC market presents a significant opportunity driven by infrastructure development, 
urbanization and increasing demand for the quality controlled concrete. Industry estimate 
indicates the market is expected to grow approximately 240 million cubic meter valued at 
INR1.25 lakhs crores in 2025 to 317 million cubic meters valued at INR1.74 lakhs crores by 
2031, representing a CAGR growth of 7% year-on-year. 
Our first RMC plant at Charholi, Pune commenced the operation on 25 September 2026, 
followed by Hoskote in Karnataka and Kalyan near Mumbai. We are progressing with a phased 
rollout across Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Chennai. 
 
The business is being led by Mr. Anil Kulkarni, an industry veteran bringing 30 years of 
experience and leadership to this business expansion. Our differentiation in the RMC business 
will be built around sustainable concrete solutions, advanced technology and customer-centric 
innovation. 
We are promoting green concrete through greater fly ash utilization, supporting the cement 
industry decarbonization effort while developing fly ash blended concrete for enhanced 
durability in conditions of water scarcity and deteriorating groundwater quality. 
 
Technology and automation will be central to our operational model, with a focus on fully 
automated, technology-enabled and manless RMC plant to address labor shortage, improve 
operational efficiency and ensure consistent quality. 
 
Alongside this, we intend to move beyond commodity-based raw material supply towards 
solution-led customized concrete offering. Tailored to specific customer needs, construction 
application and project requirements, creating a greater value through product performance and 
application expertise. 
 
To support this ambition, we are building an integrated technology platform covering batching, 
logistics, procurement and financial reporting alongside stronger capability across sales, quality 
and operations in the RMC business. We intend to create a scalable operating model with a 
commitment to 100% on-time delivery and 0 cube failure and not just individual RMC plant. 
 
Importantly, we are adopting a capital-light lease-based model that enables us to scale without 
significant investment in fixed assets. We believe this is the right way to build the business.

total installed wind capacity reached 59.2 gigawatts as on September 2026.

Energy indicating that India could add up to 8 gigawatts wind capacity during FY'27 compared 
to 6 gigawatts during  FY'26. This strong pipeline expected to support increased equipment 
demand and project activity across the wind energy value chain.

including the development of domestic manufacturing capability, while strengthening its 
leadership and execution team with experienced industry professionals to support the next phase 
of growth.

through 4 initiatives. First, governed attached supply. We are moving from own vehicle to 
driver-cum-owner model and third-party supply with the same quality and the service standard 
for every vehicle. This turns fixed ownership cost into variable payout, increasing the skin in the 
game for the drivers.
